subject: Auto-rollback on SLO breach — MVP scope + launch criteria (SRE/Release signoff)
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2026 at 4:12 PM PST
Subject: Auto-rollback on SLO breach — MVP scope + launch criteria (SRE/Release signoff)

Sean, Connor —

Following up to lock MVP scope + launch gates for auto-rollback on SLO breach. Goal is to avoid ambiguity before we start enabling beyond staging.

PRD (latest): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PROD/Auto-rollback+on+SLO+breach+integration+-+PRD
Linear: PM-612 (MVP): https://linear.app/redwood/issue/PM-612/auto-rollback-on-slo-breach-mvp

Proposed MVP scope (what we ship behind flag):
1) Signals (eligible SLO monitors)
- p95 + p99 latency burn-rate (fast + slow windows)
- 5xx error-rate burn-rate (fast + slow windows)
- Monitor staleness detection (missing/stale => no auto action; emit event + alert)

2) Evaluation semantics
- Dual-window burn-rate confirmation (fast window triggers “candidate”, slow window confirms)
- Minimum sample size gating (per-scope requests/min tokens threshold)
- Debounce/holdoff to prevent oscillation (i.e., once action taken, don’t re-evaluate for N minutes)

3) Actions
- Canary/staged rollout: auto PAUSE on confirmed breach, then auto ROLLBACK to last-known-good if breach persists for configured grace period (default 10m)
- A/B: shift traffic back to baseline (equivalent to rollback) with a rate-limited step-down

4) Auditability + surfacing
- Audit event emitted for: triggered, suppressed, missing monitor, stale monitor
- Console shows “Auto action” in rollout timeline with “why” and links to dashboards

Non-goals for MVP (explicit):
- Multi-region failover orchestration
- Quality/eval-based rollback signals

Success metrics (MVP):
- For enabled internal routes: time from breach -> pause <= 2 min (p50), <= 5 min (p95)
- Reduction in manual intervention time during canary incidents (proxy: # rollouts requiring oncall manual rollback)
- No paging storms from noisy monitors (alert volume stays within agreed thresholds)

Launch gating checklist (asking for your signoff on this set):
- Required monitors exist and are “safe” for the rollout scope (route/model/region/tier)
- Dashboards shipped + oncall has access
- Alert routing validated (notify vs page)
- Runbook complete + linked from Console
- Feature flag default OFF in prod, staged enablement plan approved

If you’re aligned, I’ll summarize this as the “MVP contract” in the PRD and we’ll use it for the Feb release train notes.

Thanks,
Marissa
Dir Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2026 at 4:36 PM PST
Subject: Re: Auto-rollback on SLO breach — MVP scope + launch criteria (SRE/Release signoff)

Aligned with the scope as written, with two SRE notes/edits for the launch gates:

1) Fail-open vs fail-closed
- Missing/stale data must be fail-open for MVP (no rollback/pause purely due to telemetry gaps), BUT we should emit an audit event + notify alert (“monitor_missing_or_stale”).
- If telemetry is degraded, auto-actions are suppressed with an explicit reason.

2) Explicit guardrails in the gate
Add to the gating checklist:
- “Min sample size configured + validated per route”: low volume services should not be eligible by default.
- “Suppression controls available”: if we’re in a known incident, oncall needs a fast way to suppress auto actions (time-bound) with justification logged.

For success metrics, I’d add one more: false positives should be trackable.
- % of auto actions where post-incident analysis says “no real regression” (we can start with tagging in the audit event and review weekly; doesn’t need to be automated day 1).

Otherwise +1.

Sean
SRE Lead (SLO semantics / oncall readiness)
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2026 at 5:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Auto-rollback on SLO breach — MVP scope + launch criteria (SRE/Release signoff)

+1 to the MVP definition.

From release side, I want to make sure the gate is written as “hard” vs “soft” requirements so we don’t end up enabling in prod without the basics.

Suggested language changes (launch gates):
HARD (must have before prod enablement for any service/route):
- Monitors present for the exact rollout scope (route/model/region/tier), checked automatically during enablement
- Dashboard + alert rule merged and deployed (observability-pack) and verified in the target env
- Runbook link present in Confluence + referenced in Console (or at least in the audit event payload)
- Feature flag + backout documented (ENG-4850) and tested in staging

SOFT (can be post-enablement follow-up but tracked):
- Console UI polish (detail panel)
- Alert copy tweaks / routing optimizations once we see real volume

Also: for Feb train, we should call out default OFF in prod with allowlist-by-route. Re: alerting, agree with Sean — notify first, page only for the oncall internal canary route.

Connor
Release Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2026 at 5:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Auto-rollback on SLO breach — MVP scope + launch criteria (SRE/Release signoff)

This is helpful — I’ll incorporate both sets of edits.

Updates I’m making to the “MVP contract” section in the PRD:
- Explicit fail-open for missing/stale telemetry (suppressed with reason + alert)
- Add suppression controls (time-bound) as a hard requirement for prod enablement
- Split launch gates into HARD vs SOFT as Connor suggested
- Add false-positive tracking as a success metric (manual tagging/review OK for MVP)

Confirming the MVP action semantics so we don’t trip later:
- Confirmed breach => auto PAUSE immediately
- If breach persists past grace period (default 10m; configurable w/ safe bounds) => auto ROLLBACK to last-known-good
- All actions behind prod feature flag, enablement by allowlist route

Sean/Connor — can you reply “Approved” if you’re good with this as the scope we hold teams to?

Marissa

Otherwise good to proceed.

Sean
